symbols.name: ReloadActiveCameraViews
symbols.source: naming pass A (NameSmithA, reviewed by NameReviewA)
symbols.evidence: The C passes the current primary camera coordinates to 0x002608 and does the same for the secondary camera only in split-screen mode. No direct catalogue caller is observed; its operations redraw existing views rather than deriving new positions.

symbols.name: EnterSplitScreen
symbols.source: naming pass A (NameSmithA, reviewed by NameReviewA)
symbols.evidence: The C optionally plays the viewport wipe and player-centering animations, sets SPLIT_SCREEN, positions both half-height cameras, and refreshes HUD/window state. The camera-mode controller at 0x00105A is its sole direct caller.

symbols.name: EnterSharedScreen
symbols.source: naming pass A (NameSmithA, reviewed by NameReviewA)
symbols.evidence: The C computes a shared camera center from both player positions and their supplied separations, clears SPLIT_SCREEN, synchronizes the second camera, and redraws the HUD and palette. It is selected by 0x00105A when the players fit within a shared viewport.

symbols.name: CenterSharedCameraOnPlayer
symbols.source: naming pass A (NameSmithA, reviewed by NameReviewA)
symbols.evidence: The C centers camera zero around the selected player, compensates for the sprite height and airborne state, and refreshes the HUD around the display-disable sequence. The camera-mode controller uses it when only one player has remaining lives.

symbols.name: PlayersRequireSeparateViews
symbols.source: naming pass A (NameSmithA, reviewed by NameReviewA)
symbols.evidence: The C returns false when either player is absent, true for different levels, and otherwise compares height-adjusted separation with 220 horizontal and 124 vertical pixels. Inventory toggling and entity movement callers use this predicate to determine whether the players require separate views.

symbols.name: UpdateScreenSplitMode
symbols.source: naming pass A (NameSmithA, reviewed by NameReviewA)
symbols.evidence: The C chooses shared, split, or single-player camera setup from player lives, level equality, menu state, and separation thresholds, using tighter thresholds to rejoin than to split. FurtherInitialisation, inventory changes, falls, and elevator transitions call it.

symbols.name: ClearCameraTileRow

symbols.evidence: The C fills all 45 words of the selected horizontal transfer buffer with the current base tile attribute and marks a 45-word row pending. The row builder at 0x0016D2 uses it for off-map rows.

symbols.name: GetLevelMetatileTile
symbols.source: naming pass A (NameSmithA, reviewed by NameReviewA)
symbols.evidence: The C reads LevelMetatileMaps[metatile][row][column], interpreting metatile bit 7 as horizontal mirroring and toggling tile flip bit 0x800. Camera row/column builders, terrain sampling, and land-animation code share this helper.

symbols.name: GetOverlayMetatileTile
symbols.source: naming pass A (NameSmithA, reviewed by NameReviewA)
symbols.evidence: The C indexes the one-based OverlayMetatileMaps set, uses metatile bit 4 for horizontal mirroring, and preserves a zero tile instead of flipping it. Camera row/column and animated-land rendering callers use zero to fall back to the base metatile.

symbols.name: BuildCameraTileRow

symbols.evidence: The packet builds a 45-word horizontal transfer row from gMapDataA or gMapDataB, preferring nonzero overlay tiles and applying the current base attributes; outside-map areas become empty or special level-border tiles. The camera redraw and direction-mask controller call it, and it sets the pending row coordinates and flag consumed by UpdateCameraY.

symbols.name: UpdateCameraFollowing

symbols.name: AnimateSplitScreenWipe
symbols.source: naming pass A (NameSmithA, reviewed by NameReviewA)
symbols.evidence: The C ensures both player sprites are resident, wipes pairs of map-plane rows inward over 15 frames, fills the split-screen destination area, and writes VDP window register 18. Entering split-screen at 0x000C2E calls it before the player-centering animation.

symbols.name: AnimatePlayersIntoSplitViews
symbols.source: naming pass A (NameSmithA, reviewed by NameReviewA)
symbols.evidence: The C interpolates both player sprites toward the centers of the two half-height viewports using 26.6 intermediates while updating sprites each frame, then restores their actual world positions. The split-screen entry routine at 0x000C2E calls it after the wipe.

symbols.name: MapRefineFilledShapeMasks
symbols.source: naming pass A (NameSmithA, reviewed by NameReviewA)
symbols.evidence: Three passes refine the low-byte shape masks of 0x0800-marked gMapDataA cells from neighboring shapes, including special handling for masks 3, 12 and 15. The C body and packet assembly agree on the mark tests and low-byte rewrites; func_003604 is the catalogued direct caller (canonical C: src/map/level_generation.c:15-82; assembly/caller packet: MapNames/packets/func_00334a.md).

symbols.name: MapBuildFilledTerrainShapes
symbols.source: naming pass A (NameSmithA, reviewed by NameReviewA)
symbols.evidence: Marks class-0x3000 cells, builds their four filled-corner bits, refines those masks through func_00334a, and selects low-byte shapes from the plain or alternate filled lookup bank. ChangeLevel calls it after region-edge generation, and the packet shows gMapDataA/gMapDataD accesses plus the direct refinement call (canonical C: src/map/level_generation.c:86-144; assembly/caller packet: MapNames/packets/func_003604.md).

symbols.name: MapBuildDirectionalPathShapes
symbols.source: naming pass A (NameSmithA, reviewed by NameReviewA)
symbols.evidence: Converts class-0x1000 cells adjoining directional class-0x2000 cells into edge shapes, then derives class-0x2000 shapes by combining their direction bits with gMapDataD low-nibble masks. The C body and packet identify ChangeLevel as its caller and MapGenerationLookupTables, gMapDataA, gMapDataD and ram_ff91ea as the controlling data (canonical C: src/map/level_generation.c:148-204; assembly/caller packet: MapNames/packets/func_0039e8.md).

symbols.name: MapScatterTerrainFeatures
symbols.source: naming pass A (NameSmithA, reviewed by NameReviewA)
symbols.evidence: Scans cells with a clear gMapDataD low nibble, inserts randomized single-cell or 2-by-2 shapes into zero-low-byte cells near class-0x1000 terrain, and substitutes selected existing shapes. ChangeLevel calls this pass; packet assembly confirms gMapDataA/gMapDataD accesses, indirect calls through a loaded GetRandomNumber address, and the func_004f50(7) generation-parameter call (canonical C: src/map/level_generation.c:208-288; assembly/caller packet: MapNames/packets/func_003cb6.md).

symbols.name: MapChooseMetatileAlternatives
symbols.source: naming pass A (NameSmithA, reviewed by NameReviewA)
symbols.evidence: Replaces every map cell with a randomly selected metatile alternative, using TileAlternativePointers for ordinary shapes and MapTransitionDescriptors for cells carrying a transition number. ChangeLevel calls it after transition assignment, and packet assembly confirms both ROM tables and GetRandomNumber calls while preserving the cell flags used by the C body (canonical C: src/map/level_generation.c:292-332; assembly/caller packet: MapNames/packets/func_004174.md).

symbols.name: MapSwapPlayerBanks
symbols.source: naming pass A (NameSmithA, reviewed by NameReviewA)
symbols.evidence: Exchanges all 26-by-19 words of gMapDataA and gMapDataB and swaps the two nibbles of each corresponding gMapDataD byte. ChangeLevel uses this when working through the other player bank, and the packet directly shows both map-bank bases and the shared byte plane (canonical C: src/map/level_generation.c:335-349; assembly/caller packet: MapNames/packets/func_00433e.md).

symbols.name: MapGetRandomGenerationParameter
symbols.source: naming pass A (NameSmithA, reviewed by NameReviewA)
symbols.evidence: Packet assembly selects a row with MapGenerationRangeRow[gLevel912A - 2], fetches the requested min/max byte pair from MapGenerationRangePairs, and returns GetRandomNumber() modulo the inclusive range plus its minimum. Its callers include ChangeLevel, the anchor-position routine, region growth and shape passes, so this is a shared generation-parameter draw rather than a terrain-specific helper; no canonical C body is present (assembly/caller packet: MapNames/packets/func_004f50.md).

symbols.name: MapCarveDirectionalPath
symbols.source: naming pass A (NameSmithA, reviewed by NameReviewA)
symbols.evidence: Walks from a supplied start cell to a target cell, ORing reciprocal direction bits and class 0x2000 into gMapDataA and conditionally copying direction bits into gMapDataD. func_004842 is its direct caller, and packet assembly confirms both map planes, the level-dependent random decisions, and indirect GetRandomNumber calls used by the C turn-selection logic (canonical C: src/map/region_walk.c:11-100; assembly/caller packet: MapNames/packets/func_004fee.md).

symbols.name: MapFindRegionGrowthOrigin
symbols.source: naming pass A (NameSmithA, reviewed by NameReviewA)
symbols.evidence: Advances a proposed 2-by-2 origin along one direction until it can extend the supplied region, rejects bounds or disallowed overlaps, and may accept overlap with another class-0x1000 region according to join_chance. It writes only the row/column output pointers on acceptance; the packet identifies func_005776 as caller and confirms gMapDataA inspection plus the random overlap decision (canonical C: src/map/region_walk.c:104-151; assembly/caller packet: MapNames/packets/func_0053c2.md).

symbols.name: MapFindInteriorGrowthOrigin
symbols.source: naming pass A (NameSmithA, reviewed by NameReviewA)
symbols.evidence: Searches along one direction for a new 2-by-2 origin whose surrounding 4-by-4 neighborhood contains only the requested region or its matching class-0x1000 base, excluding the first three anchor coordinates. The packet confirms ELEVATOR_POS_TABLE/gMapDataA reads and func_005776 as caller; accepted origins are returned through row/column pointers without modifying the map (canonical C: src/map/region_walk.c:156-199; assembly/caller packet: MapNames/packets/func_00557a.md).

symbols.name: MapGrowTerrainRegion
symbols.source: naming pass A (NameSmithA, reviewed by NameReviewA)
symbols.evidence: Packet assembly forms a class-plus-region label, writes a 2-by-2 footprint into gMapDataA, merges encountered class-0x1000 labels, and repeatedly seeks further origins through func_0053c2 or func_00557a with randomized turning and stopping decisions. ChangeLevel requests class-0x1000 coverage while func_00655a requests class 0x3000; the packet also shows generation-parameter draws and a whole-map class-coverage limit, but no canonical C body is present (assembly/caller packet: MapNames/packets/func_005776.md).

symbols.name: MapFillRectangleAndMergeRegions
symbols.source: naming pass A (NameSmithA, reviewed by NameReviewA)
symbols.evidence: Fills a supplied rectangle with a replacement map word, replacing every occurrence across gMapDataA when an overwritten class-0x1000 cell has a different region label. func_005bfe uses it through a loaded function pointer in the packet; its rectangle loops and whole-map relabeling agree with the canonical C body (canonical C: src/map/region_cleanup.c:11-27; assembly/caller packet: MapNames/packets/func_005afa.md).

symbols.name: MapExpandRegionsBesidePaths
symbols.source: naming pass A (NameSmithA, reviewed by NameReviewA)
symbols.evidence: Examines the four direction bits of one path cell and expands neighboring class-0x1000 regions into 2-by-3 or 3-by-2 rectangles through func_005afa, reporting whether anything changed. func_0064ea directly calls it for class-0x2000 cells, and packet assembly confirms four direction tests plus four indirect rectangle-helper call sites (canonical C: src/map/region_cleanup.c:31-74; assembly/caller packet: MapNames/packets/func_005bfe.md).

symbols.name: MapWidenHorizontalRegionEdges
symbols.source: naming pass A (NameSmithA, reviewed by NameReviewA)
symbols.evidence: Scans horizontal runs on the top and bottom edges of class-0x1000 regions, extends two cells into a neighboring row at the run threshold, and clears the middle cell of a sufficiently long outer-border run. func_0064ea calls this prepass; the C body and gMapDataA-only packet also preserve the counter-reset-to-one quirk rather than assuming a strict uninterrupted run (canonical C: src/map/region_cleanup.c:82-141; assembly/caller packet: MapNames/packets/func_0060ae.md).

symbols.name: MapWidenVerticalRegionEdges
symbols.source: naming pass A (NameSmithA, reviewed by NameReviewA)
symbols.evidence: Scans vertical runs on the left and right edges of class-0x1000 regions, extends two cells into a neighboring column, or clears the middle cell at the outer map border. func_0064ea calls this prepass, and the C body and gMapDataA-only packet show the same threshold/reset behavior as the horizontal pass (canonical C: src/map/region_cleanup.c:145-204; assembly/caller packet: MapNames/packets/func_0062ca.md).

symbols.name: MapStabilizeRegionConnections
symbols.source: naming pass A (NameSmithA, reviewed by NameReviewA)
symbols.evidence: Runs the horizontal and vertical edge prepasses, then repeatedly visits all class-0x2000 cells until func_005bfe reports no further expansion. ChangeLevel calls this convergence pass before its connectivity check, and packet metadata confirms the three direct helper calls and gMapDataA class test (canonical C: src/map/region_cleanup.c:207-224; assembly/caller packet: MapNames/packets/func_0064ea.md).

symbols.name: MapSeedFilledTerrainRegions
symbols.source: naming pass A (NameSmithA, reviewed by NameReviewA)
symbols.evidence: Clears temporary 0x0800 marks, finds uniform 4-by-4 areas of a region without any of the first three anchor positions, and probabilistically requests class-0x3000 growth at the inner origin. ChangeLevel calls it after connectivity succeeds; the packet confirms ELEVATOR_POS_TABLE/gMapDataA accesses, func_004f50(4), and the func_005776 growth request (canonical C: src/map/region_cleanup.c:228-268; assembly/caller packet: MapNames/packets/func_00655a.md).

symbols.name: MapBuildRegionEdgeShapes

symbols.evidence: Marks one region at a time, chooses its plain/alternate bank, computes corner masks from the four surrounding complete 2-by-2 neighborhoods, and ORs the corresponding edge shape into class-0x1000 cells. ChangeLevel supplies the region count; the C lookup-bank accesses and packet mark/alternate-bit operations show this is edge-shape construction rather than new region placement (canonical C: src/map/region_cleanup.c:272-331; assembly/caller packet: MapNames/packets/func_00671c.md).

symbols.evidence: The C terminates the secondary sentinel chain and restores the saved primary link at VRAM 0xF8BA. The viewport chain selector and ElevatorRideVBlank call it to expose primary-view entity sprites.

symbols.name: SelectSecondaryViewportSprites
symbols.source: naming pass A (NameSmithA, reviewed by NameReviewA)
symbols.evidence: The C links the primary sentinel to sentinel 24 and restores the saved secondary link at VRAM 0xF8C2. The viewport chain selector uses it for the secondary view or an inventory-swapped viewport.

symbols.name: LinkPlayerSpritesForSplitWipe
symbols.source: naming pass A (NameSmithA, reviewed by NameReviewA)
symbols.evidence: The C chains both players' primary sprite pieces together from sentinel 23 to terminator 79 and uploads the complete hardware sprite table. Only the split-screen wipe at 0x002E6A directly calls this specialized arrangement.

symbols.name: HideFlaggedPlayerSprites
symbols.source: naming pass A (NameSmithA, reviewed by NameReviewA)
symbols.evidence: The C checks the selected player's hide/blink flag and sprite readiness, then writes hardware Y=1 for every sprite in its active viewport list. HandleVBlank calls it on alternating player slots.

symbols.name: AllocateSpriteSlots
symbols.source: naming pass A (NameSmithA, reviewed by NameReviewA)
symbols.evidence: The C selects from 54 hardware-sprite allocation flags, preferring unused slots and optionally reclaiming reusable occupied ones; it returns public identifiers offset by 25 and marks the selected flags. The entity-viewport allocator and single-slot shadow allocator call it.

symbols.name: AllocateSpriteSlot
symbols.source: naming pass A (NameSmithA, reviewed by NameReviewA)
symbols.evidence: The C requests exactly one slot from the shared sprite-slot allocator and returns its identifier, or zero on failure. Process2FEntityBit0 calls it to obtain viewport shadow sprites.

symbols.name: FreeSpriteSlots
symbols.source: naming pass A (NameSmithA, reviewed by NameReviewA)
symbols.evidence: The C walks a supplied list of hardware-sprite identifiers, subtracts the base 25, and clears each allocation flag. OpeningPresents7 calls it while releasing an entity's viewport resources.

symbols.name: FreeSpriteSlot
symbols.source: naming pass A (NameSmithA, reviewed by NameReviewA)
symbols.evidence: The C subtracts the public identifier base 25 and clears one sprite allocation flag. The viewport release and shadow cleanup routines call it for individually held shadow sprites.

symbols.name: IsSpriteSlotLocked
symbols.source: naming pass A (NameSmithA, reviewed by NameReviewA)
symbols.evidence: The C returns whether bit 1 of the slot's allocation byte is set; the allocator sets that bit for non-reclaimable entity pieces but not ordinary shadow allocations. Shadow positioning/allocation/cleanup callers use it to detect that a formerly reusable shadow slot has been claimed.

symbols.name: AllocateSpriteTileRun
symbols.source: naming pass A (NameSmithA, reviewed by NameReviewA)
symbols.evidence: The C rounds a tile count up to eight-tile groups, finds a consecutive free run in the 80-byte allocation map, marks it, and returns the first tile index starting at 640. Entity viewport allocation and the map-overlay sprite helper call it.

symbols.name: FreeSpriteTileRun
symbols.source: naming pass A (NameSmithA, reviewed by NameReviewA)
symbols.evidence: The C translates a tile index relative to 640 into eight-tile group indices and clears the rounded-up allocation run. Entity viewport allocation/release and map-overlay cleanup call it.

symbols.name: ReleaseEntityShadows
symbols.source: naming pass A contradiction fix (NameReviewA accepted)
symbols.evidence: src/sprites/entity_slots_tu14.c:147-157 releases still-reusable shadow sprites and clears their handles. The dispatcher in entity_depth.c:70-74 calls this branch when draw_flags bit 6 is clear, opposite to the current label's bit-6 implication.

symbols.name: AllocateEntityViewportSprites
symbols.source: naming pass A (NameSmithA, reviewed by NameReviewA)
symbols.evidence: The C allocates an entity's tile run when needed, then claims the requested viewport's hardware sprite slots and sets the corresponding draw bit, releasing a new tile run on failure. Visibility, speech, menus, land overlays, and cutscene object setup all use it.

symbols.name: ReleaseEntityViewportSprites
symbols.source: naming pass A contradiction fix (NameReviewA accepted)
symbols.evidence: src/sprites/entity_slots_tu14.c:193-223 clears the requested viewport draw bit, releases that viewport's sprite slots and unclaimed shadow, and frees the tile run after the last viewport is removed. Visibility changes and FreeEntity call it for all entity categories; no present-opening action is performed.

symbols.name: PlayerStartFalling

symbols.evidence: Canonical C gates on gPlayer1Powerup[player] == 1, begins directional jump phases from action input, plays Sfx_Springing, and applies the spring ascent and horizontal boost. The packet identifies ProcessPlayers as its caller and confirms the fall/elevator exclusions and TOEJAM_JUMP_COUNTER/ram_ffda30/ram_ffda24 updates (source: src/player/player_states_and_respawn.c:86; packet: PlayerNames/packets/func_01062c.json).

symbols.name: PlayerResolveDescendingTerrain
symbols.source: naming pass A (NameSmithA, reviewed by NameReviewA)
symbols.evidence: Canonical C resolves descending 0x20/0x10000000 states against solid terrain, terrain 0x80, and terrain 0x90, choosing a splash, SetToejamFalling, or a landing/fall-state counter. ProcessPlayers calls it, and active spring-shoe or speed-boost powerups alter ascent cancellation and landing movement (source: src/player/player_states_and_respawn.c:137; packet: PlayerNames/packets/func_0107b2.json).

symbols.name: PlayerAdvanceToNextLevel
symbols.source: naming pass A (NameSmithA, reviewed by NameReviewA)
symbols.evidence: Canonical C waits for the object in ram_ffde56[player] to finish, unloads the current level, increments player->level, and rebuilds its map, elevator, and placed objects. Its packet shows func_010ab6 as the caller; final placement uses func_012762 or SetPositionOnNewLevel and raises the player to height 70 (source: src/player/player_states_and_respawn.c:198; packet: PlayerNames/packets/func_010968.json).

symbols.name: PlayerRelocateToPartnerOrNextLevel

ProcessInventory and func_021d32 call it; it redraws the view and initializes either a descending entry or an elevator-linked standing state, so relocation is observed without assuming a respawn-only purpose (source: src/player/player_states_and_respawn.c:231; packet: PlayerNames/packets/func_010ab6.json).

symbols.name: EarthlingLaunchControlRemapProjectile

symbols.evidence: Canonical C allocates one of four ram_ffe1d8 objects and launches it left or right from the earthling's object with the matching dat_0aeffe/dat_0af006 animation. Its packet caller is func_01d288, and the consuming func_01cd9e applies func_01cb86's player control-remap effect on impact (source: src/presents/projectile_effects.c:194; packet: PlayerNames/packets/func_01c96a.json).

symbols.name: EntityFindProjectileTargetHit

symbols.evidence: Canonical C checks active players and then active ram_ffde58 decoys on the projectile's level using horizontal reach, scaled y reach, and a height-overlap test. Func_01cd9e calls it, and the return is zero for no hit or one plus the matched entity index, not a hardware-sprite number (source: src/presents/projectile_effects.c:243; packet: PlayerNames/packets/func_01ca64.json).

symbols.name: MapReversePathDirection
symbols.source: naming pass A (NameSmithA, reviewed by NameReviewA)

symbols.source: naming pass A (NameSmithA, reviewed by NameReviewA)

symbols.evidence: Returns the low direction nibble of gMapDataD[row][column] for bank zero or the high nibble for the other bank. func_01ea66 calls it through a loaded function address in the packet, whose assembly confirms the shared byte-plane indexing and bank-dependent mask/shift (canonical C: src/map/land_processing.c:122-129; assembly/caller packet: MapNames/packets/func_01ea06.md).

symbols.name: MapConsumePathCellDirections

It returns target index+1 or zero. src/earthlings/state_dispatch_tu26.c:74-86,183-187 uses it to stop newly entered collisions and register decoy hits. symbols.name: CopyLongwordRunToVramTile
symbols.source: naming pass B (NameSmithB, reviewed by NameReviewB)
symbols.evidence: Assembly-only packets/func_026f98.json reads source pointer at entry SP+4, tile-position argument at +8 and a run argument at +12. Shifts/swap encode tile_position*32 as a VRAM write command at 0xC00004, then move.l copies source longwords to 0xC00000. The DBRA counter is run_argument<<3 with no preceding decrement, so the observed transfer is (low16(run_argument<<3)+1) longwords, not an assumed exact tile-count copy. No catalogued direct caller is reported; this is VDP transfer code, not audio or arithmetic runtime.

symbols.name: FillVdpDataWords
symbols.source: naming pass B (NameSmithB, reviewed by NameReviewB)
symbols.evidence: Assembly-only packets/func_026fc2.json loads the value and count from entry SP+4/+8, decrements the low-word count once, and repeatedly move.w stores the value to VDP data port 0xC00000 using DBRA. It does not set a VDP address command. The packet records two calls from func_03a48a. Word count zero follows the original DBRA wraparound behavior; no validation is implied.

symbols.name: FillVdpDataBytes
symbols.source: naming pass B (NameSmithB, reviewed by NameReviewB)
symbols.evidence: Assembly-only packets/func_026fd8.json has the value/count stack interface and count-minus-one DBRA loop of func_026fc2, but its repeated store to VDP data port 0xC00000 is move.b, not move.w. It neither increments a memory destination nor sets the VDP address. No direct caller is catalogued; the byte-port operation is explicitly retained instead of calling this an audio helper.

symbols.name: UploadVramWordRectangle
symbols.source: naming pass B (NameSmithB, reviewed by NameReviewB)
symbols.evidence: Assembly-only packets/func_027004.json reads VRAM byte address, sequential source pointer, words-per-row, rows, and destination row stride from entry stack slots. It doubles the stride to bytes, emits a masked VRAM write command for each destination row, streams width words from the source through 0xC00000, and uses two count-minus-one DBRA loops. SEGAVideo is its packet caller. This is a strided VRAM rectangle upload rather than a scalar math routine.

Caller role: IntroPart5 and IntroPart7 use this shared scene-mode motion updater; scene numbers are not assigned unsupported ship/meteor identities.

symbols.name: IntroDrivingActorTwoLoopAnimation

IntroPart5 selects it via func_028558(2,...,3), which installs it in the third driving actor sequence pointer. The byte program lies inside the 124-byte IntroFrameIndexLists typed data unit; tools/assets.py decodes 0xFE as hold and 0xFF as loop.

symbols.name: AudioSubmitPendingPcmSample
symbols.source: naming pass B (NameSmithB, reviewed by NameReviewB)
symbols.evidence: scratch/agents/NameSmithB/LateFunctions/packets/func_03f62a.txt, frag_03f61c.txt and MassiveRoutine.txt: reads the pending pointer gMusicUnknownE480, takes its first unsigned word as byte length, and sends the following payload pointer as three address bytes at 0xA00044..46 plus length bytes at 0xA00048..49, setting Z80 command byte 0xA00040 to 2. The high payload-address byte is also written to 0xA00042. Sets word TOEJAM_SPEECH_COUNTER to length/138+5, clears the pending pointer on success and sets gMusicUnknownE47E=-1 on success or bus timeout. The preceding fragment releases the bus and delays before busy-mailbox retries. Caller role: MassiveRoutine gives this queued-pointer path priority over pending indexed commands; PlaySoundEffect is the generic pointer/priority producer, including Jam Out drum and record-scratch samples.

symbols.name: AudioTrySubmitSequencerPcmSample
symbols.source: naming pass B (NameSmithB, reviewed by NameReviewB)
symbols.evidence: scratch/agents/NameSmithB/LateFunctions/packets/func_03f6c6.txt: accepts a stack sample pointer only while TOEJAM_SPEECH_COUNTER and alternate-template flag ram_ffe476 are zero. Requests the Z80 bus with a bounded acknowledgement loop, releases/delays/retries when mailbox byte 0xA00041 is busy, rejects nonzero 0xA0004B, then submits the word-length-prefixed payload through address bytes 0xA00044..46, length 0xA00048..49 and command 2 at 0xA00040. Unlike func_03f62a it does not set the generic PCM holdoff word or consume the queued pointer. Caller role: MassiveRoutine sequence commands pass Sfx_JamRecordScratch, Sfx_JamClap, Sfx_JamBassDrum and Sfx_JamSnareDrum here as background/music percussion.

symbols.name: MapBoundaryShapesPlain
symbols.source: naming pass B (NameSmithB, reviewed by NameReviewB)
symbols.evidence: include/assets_map.h declares unsigned char[20]. src/map/level_generation.c:func_0039e8 selects replacement 16,17,18,19 according to class-2 neighbors above/right/below/left and ORs this lookup byte into the cleared low byte of a class-1 cell when bit 0x8000 is clear. Observed entries 16..19 are 17,18,19,20; entries 0..15 are declared but not read by this consumer. It is a subview at +0x10 of the 196-byte MapGenerationLookupTables ROM unit (data_units.json), not a separately proved 20-byte allocation. include/map.h identifies the exact alias MapGenerationLookupTables.edge_plain[20] (offset 0x10).

symbols.name: MapBoundaryShapesAlternate
symbols.source: naming pass B (NameSmithB, reviewed by NameReviewB)
symbols.evidence: include/assets_map.h declares unsigned char[20]. src/map/level_generation.c:func_0039e8 selects indices 16..19 from adjacent class-2 direction bits and ORs the table byte into class-1 cells carrying 0x8000; this is the alternate-bank counterpart of dat_08bf5a. Observed values at 16..19 are 41,42,43,44. The declared 20-byte view begins +0x24 inside the 196-byte MapGenerationLookupTables unit; no independent allocation boundary is established. include/map.h identifies the exact alias MapGenerationLookupTables.edge_alternate[20] (offset 0x24).

symbols.name: MapPathTurnDirections
symbols.source: naming pass B (NameSmithB, reviewed by NameReviewB)
symbols.evidence: include/assets_map.h declares unsigned char[] with no bound. src/map/region_walk.c:func_004fee reads [direction+1+random%3] for direction bits 1(up),2(right),4(down),8(left), so the observed union of indices is 2..11; returned values select a non-reversing walk and reciprocal map bits. include/map.h explicitly gives the aliased MapGenerationLookupTables.direction_choices[12] at offset 0x78, establishing the 12-byte field view while not proving an independent allocation; byte values are 0,1,2,4,8,1,2,8,0,1,2,4.

symbols.name: LargeItemExcludedTerrainIds
symbols.source: naming pass B (NameSmithB, reviewed by NameReviewB)
symbols.evidence: include/assets_map.h declares char[23]. src/presents/level_item_setup.c:func_01454a masks terrain with 0x7f and scans all 23 bytes for equality; LoadLevel2AndUp excludes a matching metatile only when large is nonzero before TerrainValidation(width=4,height=2). Observed IDs are 12..25,47..50,59..63. A following zero byte precedes the next table but is not part of the 23-entry scanned view; this is a subview inside the 196-byte MapGenerationLookupTables unit. include/map.h aliases it as MapGenerationLookupTables.present_terrain[23] at 0x84, followed by reserved_9b.

symbols.name: ControlRemapDirections
symbols.source: naming pass B (NameSmithB, reviewed by NameReviewB)
symbols.evidence: include/assets_map.h declares unsigned char[4][10] (40 bytes). src/presents/projectile_effects.c:func_01cc62 reads [ram_ffe1e2[player]][(input&15)-1] when directional input is nonzero, then combines the returned direction nibble with input&240; func_01cb86 chooses the first index with random&3. Valid single/diagonal pad combinations address columns 0..9; the code does not bound arbitrary impossible direction masks. Exact 4x10 stride and 40-byte final subview are within MapGenerationLookupTables; no extra extent is inferred. include/map.h aliases it as MapGenerationLookupTables.input_directions[4][10] at offset 0x9c.

symbols.name: SingleFrameHoldAnimation
symbols.source: naming pass B (NameSmithB, reviewed by NameReviewB)
symbols.evidence: include/assets_presents.h:19-21 explicitly retains char[] views rom_0ae4a0 and dat_0ae4a0 for the same bytes at 0x0AE4A0; these two proposal records deliberately share a name/storage. SetupPlayer in src/player/setup_player.c:62-83 uses the rom_ spelling for selector and six-present display chains. The decoded SharedAnimationPrograms container (176 bytes at 0x0AE474) has frame 0 followed by hold at offsets 44/45, proving a two-byte program, not an independent 176-byte alias allocation. Other dat_ consumers include ground items, stolen presents, and idle telephones. tools/assets.py:663-665,737-739 establishes one byte per animation command: the two stored values are 0x00 and 0xFE.

symbols.name: Player1LifeRequestDisplayAnimation
symbols.source: naming pass B (NameSmithB, reviewed by NameReviewB)
symbols.evidence: MatchWave23/src/earthlings/nice_earthling_touch.c declares an incomplete struct timed_animation[] and reads sequence, frames and period from element zero when building the life-request display. Canonical src/earthlings/nice_earthling_touch.c:410-416 replaces this view with &PlayerAnimationDescriptors[5]: the aliases identify one target ten-byte descriptor, not an independent array. The typed 268-record PlayerAnimationDescriptors container places it at offset 5*10 from 0x0AE524; decoded fields are the shared 0x0AE476 sequence, Spr_ToejamGhost frame table, period 7 and spare 0. Only this record is observed through the old spelling.

symbols.name: Player2AnimationDescriptors
symbols.source: naming pass B (NameSmithB, reviewed by NameReviewB)
symbols.evidence: include/assets_sprites.h declares struct timed_animation[121], ten target bytes per entry (two four-byte pointers, period byte and y-offset/spare byte). SetupPlayer in setup_player.c:49-61 explicitly uses index 0 for the second player, SetSprite in sprites/set_sprite.c:13-25 uses this bank whenever entity_number!=0 and copies the runtime-selected record, and nice_earthling_touch.c:410-416 uses index 5 for its life-request display. data_units.json partitions the enclosing 268 records as 121+121+13+13, establishing this second 121-record/1210-byte bank. Index 5 is the same storage as dat_0aea10; SetSprite itself supplies no upper-bound validation.

symbols.name: Player2LifeRequestDisplayAnimation
symbols.source: naming pass B (NameSmithB, reviewed by NameReviewB)
symbols.evidence: MatchWave23/src/earthlings/nice_earthling_touch.c declares an incomplete struct timed_animation[] and reads sequence, frames and period from its first record for player_number!=0. Canonical nice_earthling_touch.c:410-416 uses &rom_0ae9de[5] for exactly the same storage. The typed PlayerAnimationDescriptors container places it at overall record 126, the second character bank record 5: one target ten-byte descriptor with shared 0x0AE476 sequence, Spr_EarlGhost frames, period 7 and spare 0. The address-spelled array declaration proves no larger independent extent.

symbols.name: ElevatorPrimaryAnimations
symbols.source: naming pass B (NameSmithB, reviewed by NameReviewB)
symbols.evidence: include/assets_sprites.h declares struct timed_animation[13], target ten-byte elements. src/elevator/elevator_scene.c:31-67 indexes by elevator state and copies sequence/frames/period into the primary entity. data_units.json groups these as records 242..254 of the larger 268-record PlayerAnimationDescriptors unit; this bank is exactly 13 records/130 bytes, not a separate 268-element array. Decoded examples are Spr_ElevatorLights at period 6 and Spr_ElevatorDepart at periods 4/3. The companion bank starts at dat_0aef1a; runtime state indexing alone does not validate every possible state value.

symbols.name: ElevatorSecondaryAnimations
symbols.source: naming pass B (NameSmithB, reviewed by NameReviewB)
symbols.evidence: include/assets_sprites.h declares struct timed_animation[13], target ten-byte records. src/elevator/elevator_scene.c:58-67 reads the selected record into the secondary entity (primary entity+2), including byte 9 as y_offset added to the primary y. data_units.json and decoded PlayerAnimationDescriptors records 255..267 establish a 13-record/130-byte bank inside that shared container. Most y_offset values are 10, with final record 0; observed period examples are 10,6,4. The bank contains animation records, not raw frames or an independent allocation inferred from adjacent addresses.

symbols.name: PlayerDecoyAnimations
symbols.source: naming pass B (NameSmithB, reviewed by NameReviewB)
symbols.evidence: include/assets_sprites.h declares struct timed_animation[2]. OpenDecoy in src/presents/present_effects.c:81-113 selects index player_number (0/1), copying sequence, frames and period. The typed 90-byte AnimationDescriptors_0AEF9C unit identifies this as records 1..2: exactly two target ten-byte descriptors/20 bytes at an interior alias, not the full enclosing nine-record bank. Decoded frames are Spr_DecoyToejam and Spr_DecoyEarl, both sharing the 0x0D8BE6 sequence and period 7.

symbols.name: HealthDrainDisplayAnimation
symbols.source: naming pass B (NameSmithB, reviewed by NameReviewB)
symbols.evidence: include/assets_sprites.h uses incomplete struct timed_animation[]; PerformPromotion in src/presents/present_effects.c:351-370 reads only element zero when promotion==16. BummerLifePromo:417-440 drains health and then sets health to zero for that display state. data_units.json places this view at record 3 of AnimationDescriptors_0AEF9C: one target ten-byte descriptor, decoded Spr_TotalBummerParticles frames and period 4. No loop or declaration through this alias proves an array beyond this record; the 90-byte containing unit is not its independent extent.

symbols.name: ExtraLifeDisplayAnimation
symbols.source: naming pass B (NameSmithB, reviewed by NameReviewB)
symbols.evidence: include/assets_sprites.h declares incomplete struct timed_animation[]. PerformPromotion in present_effects.c:351-371 uses the first descriptor for the non-11/non-16 display; examined callers pass 11,16,17, and BummerLifePromo:431-435 grants the life for sprite_state 17. The typed AnimationDescriptors_0AEF9C bank places the alias at record 4, one target ten-byte descriptor; decoded frames are Spr_ExtraLiveParticles, period 4. Only one descriptor is observed through this spelling, not an inferred suffix allocation.

symbols.name: RankPromotionDisplayAnimation
symbols.source: naming pass B (NameSmithB, reviewed by NameReviewB)
symbols.evidence: include/assets_sprites.h declares incomplete struct timed_animation[]. PerformPromotion in present_effects.c:351-370 reads its first sequence/frames/period for promotion 11, creating the two-sprite 32-tile display; BummerLifePromo later announces RankNameStrTable[gPlayerRank]. The typed 90-byte AnimationDescriptors_0AEF9C unit places this as record 5, one target ten-byte descriptor with decoded Spr_PromotionFireworks frames and period 3. Larger array/allocation extent is not established by this view.

symbols.name: DoorwayAnimations
symbols.source: naming pass B (NameSmithB, reviewed by NameReviewB)
symbols.evidence: include/assets_sprites.h declares incomplete struct timed_animation[]. PresentIsDoorway installs index 0, and func_0161aa in present_effects.c:295-315 selects index active where active is 0 or 1, copying sequence/frames/period. The typed AnimationDescriptors_0AEF9C container places these at records 6 and 7, proving two target ten-byte records/20 bytes of observed view, not the complete 90-byte bank. Both decoded periods are 0 and both sequences point to the single-frame hold program; the frame tables distinguish the two doorway states.

symbols.name: TransientEffectAnimation
symbols.source: naming pass B (NameSmithB, reviewed by NameReviewB)
symbols.evidence: include/assets_sprites.h declares one struct timed_animation scalar. func_015b66 in present_effects.c:48-79 copies its sequence/frames/period into the per-player short-lived entity; land_path_animation.c:30-44 reuses the same sequence/frames for eight path animations but explicitly overrides phase to 2. The typed AnimationDescriptors_0AEF9C unit identifies record 8, exactly ten bytes; decoded frames are Spr_Poof and period 2. This is shared descriptor storage, not a different animation allocation for each consumer.

symbols.name: ControlRemapProjectileLeftAnimation
symbols.source: naming pass B (NameSmithB, reviewed by NameReviewB)
symbols.evidence: include/assets_sprites.h declares a scalar struct animation_descriptor: only two target four-byte pointers (eight bytes), not timed_animation. func_01c96a in projectile_effects.c:215-235 uses it when earthling state==10, launching from x-22 at velocity_x=-896 and hardcoding frame_phase=9. The typed AnimationDescriptors_0AEFF6 unit contains three eight-byte records; this alias is record 1 at offset 8, with decoded Spr_CupidArrow frames and sequence 0x0AE4A5. No period byte belongs to this record.

symbols.name: ControlRemapProjectileRightAnimation
symbols.source: naming pass B (NameSmithB, reviewed by NameReviewB)
symbols.evidence: include/assets_sprites.h declares one eight-byte struct animation_descriptor sequence/frame-table pair. func_01c96a in projectile_effects.c:215-235 chooses it for the non-state-10 launch, placing x+22 and velocity_x=896, and supplies phase 9 in code. data_units.json places it at record 2/offset 16 of the 24-byte AnimationDescriptors_0AEFF6 unit; decoded frames are Spr_CupidArrow and sequence 0x0AE4FD. This is the final eight-byte pair, not a ten-byte timed descriptor or independent three-entry table.

symbols.name: TomatoTargetImpactAnimation
symbols.source: naming pass B (NameSmithB, reviewed by NameReviewB)
symbols.evidence: include/assets_sprites.h declares one target ten-byte struct timed_animation. ProcessTomatoRain in projectile_effects.c:90-113 installs its sequence/frames/period after func_025e72 reports a hit and stops projectile velocities, using frame=-1/duration=1. The typed 50-byte AnimationDescriptors_0AF00E unit places it at record 1, not the whole five-record bank; decoded frames are Spr_TomatoSplat and period 4. The name is tied to the observed tomato-pool hit path.

symbols.name: TomatoGroundImpactAnimation
symbols.source: naming pass B (NameSmithB, reviewed by NameReviewB)
symbols.evidence: include/assets_sprites.h declares a scalar target ten-byte struct timed_animation. ProcessTomatoRain in projectile_effects.c:59-85 selects it when an airborne tomato lands at height<=0 on terrain other than 128 or the separately handled 144, then zeros motion and copies sequence/frames/period. The typed AnimationDescriptors_0AF00E bank places this at record 2; decoded frames are Spr_TomatoPlop and period 4. Only this ten-byte record is observed at the alias; no guessed terrain identity is encoded in the name.

symbols.name: TomatoTerrain128ImpactAnimation
symbols.source: naming pass B (NameSmithB, reviewed by NameReviewB)
symbols.evidence: include/assets_sprites.h declares one target ten-byte struct timed_animation. ProcessTomatoRain in projectile_effects.c:59-85 chooses it specifically for terrain result 128 at a landed tomato, clears movement, and copies sequence/frames/period with frame=-1/duration=1. The typed AnimationDescriptors_0AF00E unit places it at record 3, decoded Spr_TomatoSplash frames and period 4. Terrain 128 is retained descriptively; identifying that terrain beyond the examined operation would be [INFERENCE].

symbols.name: TimedEntityEffectAnimation
symbols.source: naming pass B (NameSmithB, reviewed by NameReviewB)
symbols.evidence: include/assets_sprites.h declares one target ten-byte struct timed_animation. src/player/effect_slots.c:25-59 installs sequence/frames/period into one of two available effect entities, at height 5, 32-by-32, and plays sound 14; func_01bea6 releases it when frame_duration becomes zero. The typed AnimationDescriptors_0AF00E unit places it at record 4, decoded Spr_Pop frames and period 4. Only one descriptor is observed at this alias; the neutral name follows the owning timed-effect slots rather than guessing the visual event.

symbols.name: PlayerRainCloudAnimations
symbols.source: naming pass B (NameSmithB, reviewed by NameReviewB)
symbols.evidence: include/assets_sprites.h declares incomplete struct timed_animation[]. PresentIsRainCloud installs index 0; func_016aca in present_effects.c:507-559 alternates index 0 idle and index 1 strike, copies sequence/frames/period, and applies the strike/recovery behavior. data_units.json places the alias at record 1 of the three-record AnimationDescriptors_0AF050 unit: the observed two-record suffix is 20 bytes, not all 30. Decoded idle/strike frame tables are Spr_RainCloudIdle (period 4) and Spr_RainCloudZap (period 2).

symbols.name: RetiringTerrainEffectAnimation
symbols.source: naming pass B (NameSmithB, reviewed by NameReviewB)
symbols.evidence: include/assets_sprites.h declares one target ten-byte struct timed_animation. func_01cf66 in projectile_effects.c:419-439 transfers the current ram_ffe1e4 handle to ram_ffe1e6 and installs this sequence/frames/period; func_01d084 removes that entity when its animation ends. data_units.json places it at record 1 of the 30-byte AnimationDescriptors_0AF076 unit, decoded Spr_Rosebush frames, period 4. The name describes its concrete retiring-effect owner without relying on a guessed present identity.

symbols.name: TemporaryTerrainEffectAnimation
symbols.source: naming pass B (NameSmithB, reviewed by NameReviewB)
symbols.evidence: include/assets_sprites.h declares one target ten-byte struct timed_animation. func_01cfea in projectile_effects.c:441-470 allocates an entity at the player position in ram_ffe1e6, assigns this sequence/frames/period, and uses dimensions 24-by-20; func_01d084 frees it at animation completion. The typed AnimationDescriptors_0AF076 unit places it at record 2, decoded Spr_Rosebush frames and period 4. It is a ten-byte interior record, not another 30-byte bank; temporary describes observed lifetime, not botanical/lore interpretation.

symbols.name: PauseDisplayAnimation
symbols.source: naming pass B (NameSmithB, reviewed by NameReviewB)
symbols.evidence: include/assets_sprites.h declares one struct animation_descriptor, an eight-byte target sequence/frame-table pair with no period field. GamePaused in src/ui/pause.c:74-102 copies its two pointers into the pause entity, sets frame=-1/duration=1, and allocates its viewport sprites. The typed 16-byte AnimationDescriptors_0AF0A8 unit places this at pair index 1, decoded single-frame hold sequence 0x0AE4A0 and Spr_Pause frames. Its eight-byte extent must not be widened to a timed-animation record.

symbols.name: gControllerButtonsAcSwapped
symbols.source: naming pass B (NameSmithB, reviewed by NameReviewB)
symbols.evidence: include/ram_system.h declares a scalar char (one observed byte). src/core/vdp_startup.c:MovePadInputIntoD0 preserves input&0x9f and exchanges masks 0x40 and 0x20 when this flag is nonzero. GetCtrl1Input packet 0x02707E proves standard pad packing (TH-low A/Start shifted into bits 6/7; TH-high B/C retained at bits 4/5). The typed MenuControllerOptionsItemsStrings ROM unit at 0x0243EA..0x02443E labels standard A=Action, B=Present List, C=Map and variation A=Map, C=Action. Thus the flag swaps A/C, not B/C; the existing vdp_startup.c comment and raw CoreGlobals slice proposal are contradicted by the bit operations/menu labels. MatchWave24/main_menu.c stores the menu selection into this byte. No larger allocation or direction-remap table is inferred.

symbols.name: gMapDirectionalPathMode

symbols.evidence: include/ram_map.h declares scalar char (one byte). src/map/level_generation.c:func_0039e8 forces gMapDataD low-nibble corners to zero when set; src/map/map_drawing.c:func_0078a8 assigns palette 3 to cells whose low path nibble is nonzero, while DisplayMap returns early and omits cover blocks. symbols.name: gMapVisitedCoverBits
symbols.source: naming pass B (NameSmithB, reviewed by NameReviewB)
symbols.evidence: include/ram_map.h declares unsigned char[26][7]; its comment explicitly marks the 26-row extent [INFERENCE] from the next table, not a proved allocation boundary. src/core/main_loop.c:ProcessInput indexes [entity->level][(y-8)>>8], ORs 0x80>>((x-72)/320), and awards a point the first time a bit is set. src/map/map_drawing.c:DisplayMap reads seven row bytes and eight bits per level to omit already visited cover blocks. Seven-byte level stride is observed; consumers do not locally bound arbitrary entity level indices. Registry gDiscoveredMapMask at 0xFF91F3 is an interior label at [1][0], not an alternative base; gTransparentMapMask at 0xFF92A0 lies inside the declared tail and carries an explicitly unverified conflicting legacy extent.

symbols.name: gMapRevealedCoverBits
symbols.source: naming pass B (NameSmithB, reviewed by NameReviewB)
symbols.evidence: include/ram_map.h declares unsigned char[26][7] (182-byte view). src/map/map_drawing.c:DisplayMap reads [level][row] for row 0..6 and bit 0x80>>column for column 0..7; existing bits retain revealed cover-block sprites, and newly selected blocks OR the bit so it remains revealed on revisits. Selection uses ram_ff935a and terrain eligibility; ProcessInput writes the separate visited table ram_ff91ec. Seven-byte level stride and seven rows of eight bits are directly observed; all 26 rows are not scanned here, so an independent 182-byte allocation is not established. Legacy gTransparentMapMask at 0xFF92A0 is two bytes before this actual C base and must not silently be conflated with it.

symbols.name: gHudDisplayedHealth
symbols.source: naming pass B contradiction fix (NameReviewB accepted)
symbols.evidence: src/ui/hud_health_update.c:func_00b18c computes the actual capacity independently as23(player0) or31(player1)+4*rank, clamps real health against that capacity, then increments/decrements TOEJAMS_MAX_HEALTH[player] one step toward real health and draws its current value. include/ram_player.h retains char[]; two player bytes observed, with no independent larger allocation inferred. src/ui/hud_status.c:HealthAndLivesChecks waits for this displayed value to reach zero before starting death. Therefore the existing max-health assertion is contradicted by the observed animated current-health cache. This repeats the already documented NameSmithA contradiction, not a new finding.

symbols.name: gHudDisplayedLives
symbols.source: naming pass B (NameSmithB, reviewed by NameReviewB)
symbols.evidence: include/ram_player.h declares char[] with no finite bound; player-number callers establish two observed byte elements 0 and 1, not a proved independent allocation. src/ui/hud_health_update.c:func_00b18c compares cached byte with gPlayerLives[player] and calls func_00b3e4/func_00b590 if changed. Packet func_00b3e4 (0x00B3E4) draws life-icon tiles then stores the current lives byte at ram_ffa256[player] (0x00B584). It is the cached displayed lives value, not health or health capacity; distinct from neighboring TOEJAMS_MAX_HEALTH displayed-health array.

symbols.name: gSpriteTileBufferOffset
symbols.source: naming pass B contradiction fix (NameReviewB accepted)
symbols.evidence: include/ram_sprites.h declares unsigned short scalar, not an array or record. src/sprites/copy_sprite_tiles.c:ClearLOC_00FFB8DA uses it as byte offset into ram_ffb8da, copies tile_count*8 longwords and adds tile_count<<5; SpriteLoadingStuff clears the word after draining upload runs. Sprite decompression/frame packets, elevator/ship C and cutscene text increment it by packed32-byte tile payload sizes. The table assertion is contradicted by a two-byte byte-offset cursor into a separate buffer. ram_ffb8da[8192] is only an inferred available span up to this word, not a proven allocator capacity. This repeats NameSmithA's gSpriteTileBufferOffset vocabulary.

symbols.name: gSpriteTileUploadRuns
symbols.source: naming pass B (NameSmithB, reviewed by NameReviewB)
symbols.evidence: include/ram_sprites.h declares unsigned short[40] (80-byte view). Packet func_00c7a8 appends destination tile and width*height tile count using two ram_ffd92e postincrements; packet func_00c920 coalesces entity pieces into the same two-word run format. src/elevator/elevator_scene.c:func_013160 appends (1,64); ship func_01fb40 appends (1,128); text func_027c64 appends (tile_base,32). SpriteLoadingStuff iterates queue_index+=2, converts destination tile<<5 to byte VRAM address and tile count<<4 to word count, advancing source through the packed tile buffer. Declared forty-word/twenty-pair capacity is not bounds-checked by these appenders; do not infer a larger allocation from the byte cursor.

symbols.evidence: include/ram_effects.h declares incomplete char[]. func_01cec2 in projectile_effects.c:388-417 writes an allocated entity index positioned at the player x,y-1 with AnimationDescriptors_0AF076[0]. func_01d084 reads that entity for nearby damage and func_01cf66 transfers its handle to ram_ffe1e6 while clearing this byte when the effect ends or changes terrain. Cleanup and player indices 0/1 establish two observed byte handles, not a finite bound inferred solely from the next array.

symbols.name: gPlayerOneShotTerrainEffectEntities
symbols.source: naming pass B (NameSmithB, reviewed by NameReviewB)

symbols.name: gPresentDisplayPanelDrawn
symbols.source: naming pass B (NameSmithB, reviewed by NameReviewB)
symbols.evidence: include/ram_ui.h declares a char scalar (one byte). func_01da0a in effects_and_inventory_display.c:174-196 returns immediately if it is nonzero, otherwise draws the five-by-nineteen PresentDisplayTilemap into VRAM, translating horizontal-flip bit 0x80 to 0x800, and then stores 1. Funkatron interactions call the drawer. The observed storage is the one-time panel-drawn latch, not the tilemap itself or an array of player flags.

symbols.name: gSpeechBubbleEntities
symbols.source: naming pass B (NameSmithB, reviewed by NameReviewB)
symbols.evidence: include/ram_speech.h declares char[4]. GenerateSpeech in speech_core.c:39-65 searches four slots, optionally frees an attached bubble for the speaker or replaces the lowest-lifetime slot, then stores an allocated bubble entity index. speech_update.c:22-29 decrements the parallel lifetime and frees/clears expired or invisible bubbles; cleanup and eviction also loop indices 0..3. The declared and observed extent is four one-byte handles, not four object_state records.

symbols.name: gSpeechBubbleLifetimes
symbols.source: naming pass B (NameSmithB, reviewed by NameReviewB)
symbols.evidence: include/ram_speech.h declares char[4]. GenerateSpeech in speech_core.c:53-58 chooses the lowest lifetime when all four bubble handles are occupied and :101-105 stores either low-byte override ram_ffe207 or default 40. speech_update.c:22-29 pre-decrements each occupied slot and frees the bubble when the signed byte becomes negative. All four indices are explicitly observed; these four byte countdowns are separate storage from the handle array, not a larger inferred span.

symbols.name: gReunionDialoguePending
symbols.source: naming pass B (NameSmithB, reviewed by NameReviewB)
symbols.evidence: include/ram_speech.h declares one char scalar. speech_update.c:46-71 sets it to 1 when levels differ or the players separate by more than 640 horizontally/448 vertically; when it is set, the players share a non-split view and approach within 260-by-174, it starts dialogue 1/3/4 and clears the byte. func_01e2c4 clears it with pending speech. Exactly one shared byte latch is observed, not a per-player timer.

symbols.name: gDelayedSpeechReplyTimers
symbols.source: naming pass B (NameSmithB, reviewed by NameReviewB)
symbols.evidence: include/ram_speech.h declares short[2], four target bytes, and explicitly aliases element [1] at 0xFFE1FA as the existing gPlayer1TomatoRainThrottle. The context packet func_01e38e selects one of two free word slots and writes DialogueDescriptors delay word +6; speech_update.c:31-34 decrements both and generates the corresponding queued text/speaker at zero. speech_core.c:122-123 clears both words through the base and alias. Two slots are declaration- and loop-proven; the alias is not a separate one-byte tomato-rain allocation.

symbols.name: gSecondSpeechReplyTimer
symbols.source: naming pass B contradiction fix (NameReviewB accepted)
symbols.evidence: Corroborates the existing NameSmithA flag, not a new independent replacement. The registry declares this RAM symbol size 1, while include/ram_speech.h explicitly aliases it as the short ram_ffe1f8[1]. speech_core.c:122-123 clears the two delayed-reply words using base [0] plus this alias, and :141-142 pairs the alias with second reply speaker ram_ffe205. speech_update.c:31-34 decrements both short reply timers and emits their queued dialogue. The examined word-width reader/writers contradict tomato-rain and player-one semantics as well as the one-byte registry extent.

symbols.name: gPlayer2TomatoRainThrottle
symbols.evidence: RAM address declared by upstream header; storage width is carried only where documented.

symbols.name: gDelayedSpeechReplyTexts
symbols.source: naming pass B (NameSmithB, reviewed by NameReviewB)
symbols.evidence: include/ram_speech.h declares char *[2]: two target four-byte text pointers/eight bytes, not characters or two text buffers. packets/func_01e38e.json writes the selected DialogueDescriptors reply pointer (+8) at slot*4; speech_update.c:31-34 passes the paired pointer to GenerateSpeech when ram_ffe1f8[slot] reaches zero. Two slots are explicitly observed. The pointed-to strings have their own ROM storage; no string extent or allocation is inferred here.

symbols.name: gDelayedSpeechReplySpeakers
symbols.source: naming pass B (NameSmithB, reviewed by NameReviewB)
symbols.evidence: include/ram_speech.h declares char[2] and aliases [1] with scalar ram_ffe205. packets/func_01e38e.json writes either the descriptor fixed speaker, caller speaker or caller^1 into the chosen byte slot; speech_update.c:31-34 passes the matching byte with queued reply text to GenerateSpeech. speech_core.c:141-142 searches both timer/speaker slots. Exactly two byte speaker indices are established; slot number is not necessarily player identity and the scalar alias adds no allocation.

symbols.name: gSecondDelayedSpeechReplySpeaker
symbols.source: naming pass B (NameSmithB, reviewed by NameReviewB)
symbols.evidence: include/ram_speech.h declares a char scalar and explicitly identifies it as ram_ffe204[1], the same storage at 0xFFE205. speech_core.c:141-143 pairs it with the second reply timer gPlayer1TomatoRainThrottle when checking for a speaker pending speech. func_01e38e writes through the base and speech_update reads both slots. Its extent is one byte within the two-speaker array, not an independent player-two field; values can name the chosen reply speaker, not merely index 1.

symbols.name: gNextSpeechLifetimeOverride
symbols.source: naming pass B (NameSmithB, reviewed by NameReviewB)
symbols.evidence: include/ram_speech.h declares a short scalar, a two-byte target word. func_01e012 in speech_core.c:17-22 writes the requested lifetime; GenerateSpeech:101-105 tests the word, copies only low-byte alias ram_ffe207 into one char lifetime slot, and clears the entire word, otherwise choosing 40. Thus it is a one-use word override whose stored bubble lifetime is truncated to its low byte, not a two-element byte array. ram_ffe207 is overlapping storage, not an extra allocation.

symbols.name: gNextSpeechLifetimeOverrideLowByte
symbols.source: naming pass B (NameSmithB, reviewed by NameReviewB)
symbols.evidence: include/ram_speech.h explicitly declares char ram_ffe207 as the low byte of the short ram_ffe206 on the big-endian target. GenerateSpeech in speech_core.c:101-104 copies this byte to ram_ffe1f2[slot] when the enclosing word is nonzero, then zeroes that word. The observed extent is one byte aliasing address 0xFFE206+1; it is not an independent lifetime field, and no second allocation or full-word copy is implied.

symbols.name: gShipPieceLevelAssignments
symbols.source: naming pass B (NameSmithB, reviewed by NameReviewB)
symbols.evidence: include/ram_ship.h declares char[10], ten byte piece-to-level assignments. func_01f98e in piece_level_assignment.c:13-40 writes fixed-world levels or distinct random levels 2..25 and forces one assignment to 25. ShipPieceAbility, func_0204ce and func_020e2a read the ten entries; GamePaused in pause.c:139-156 clears assignments and can move the remaining one. Zero denotes an already absent/collected assignment. This storage is distinct from the misleading existing gShipPieceLevels ship-display block at 0xFFE21C; no extra ten-byte allocation is inferred.

symbols.name: gShipScreenState
symbols.source: naming pass B contradiction fix (NameReviewB accepted)
symbols.evidence: Corroborates the existing NameSmithA flag. include/ram_ship.h declares this separate ten-byte ship-display block and aliases bytes [2]/[6] as ram_ffe21e/ram_ffe222. screen_setup.c:54-98 uses [0] as background frame 1/2 and [2] as a twelve-tick countdown; piece_collection.c:58-84 consumes [4] as a pending piece display request and [6] as an entity handle. The actual ten piece-to-level assignments are independently declared at ram_ffe212[10] and populated in piece_level_assignment.c:13-40. The address therefore names display state, not piece-level assignments.

symbols.source: naming pass B (NameSmithB, reviewed by NameReviewB)

symbols.name: gMailboxLevelStates
symbols.source: naming pass B (NameSmithB, reviewed by NameReviewB)
symbols.evidence: include/ram_earthlings.h declares struct special_earthling_state[2]. include/earthlings.h:54-60 proves six target bytes per record: char mode, char level, short timer, char contact[2], so the declared view is two records/twelve bytes. func_020eaa initializes both banks by level, selects mode 1 with the observed 50-percent rule and clears two contact bytes otherwise. func_020e70 reads matching level/non-one mode, and AI_MailboxTouch uses mode to choose mail order versus attacking animation, decrements the word timer (33/175), and advances per-player contact states 0/1/2. These are bank records, not two Earthling object_state records.

symbols.name: gPcmEffectCooldownTicks
symbols.source: naming pass B contradiction fix (NameReviewB accepted)
symbols.evidence: The word is not a ToeJam speech/bubble counter. Packet func_03f62a loads the queued PCM sample header count, computes count/138+5 and stores that software cooldown here after submitting the sample to Z80; MassiveRoutine decrements it each service tick. PlaySoundEffect tests it during priority arbitration, and func_03f6c6 blocks music-triggered PCM while it is nonzero. Canonical src/ship/screen_setup.c:219-230 uses the same word to serialize clap, hallelujah and jammin samples; src/earthlings/nice_earthling_touch.c:152-153 and generic_enemy_tu27.c:45-47 gate mailbox roar/dentist laugh, and src/player/sleep.c:91-92 gates snoring. None of these paths selects a ToeJam speech entity. The declared short scalar/2-byte view in include/ram_speech.h belongs to the general PCM-effect cooldown state; the present header grouping is misleading too. Private independent packets: SceneGlobals/packets/func_03f62a.md, func_03ed6e.md, func_03f5dc.md and func_03f6c6.md. Independently corroborated by LateFunctions/contradictions.json and LateFunctions/packets; that slice suggests the synonymous gPcmPlaybackHoldoff, while the root standardizes gPcmEffectCooldownTicks.
